Compare co-expression networks across species in one call

Source: R/rcomplex.R
rcomplex.Rd

rcomplex() runs the whole analysis. It builds one network per species, tests every ortholog pair in every species pair, and classifies the gene cliques. Give it expression or networks, plus orthologs.

Usage

rcomplex(
  expr = NULL,
  orthologs,
  networks = NULL,
  block = NULL,
  clades = NULL,
  density = 0.03,
  sign = c("positive", "negative"),
  method = c("hypergeometric", "rank"),
  alpha = 0.1,
  modules = FALSE,
  null = FALSE,
  n_cores = 1L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

expr

Named list of expression data, one entry per species: a genes x samples matrix or a SummarizedExperiment. Give expr or networks, not both.

orthologs

The long ortholog table (species, gene, hog), or a path to an ortholog file for read_orthologs().

networks

Named list of network objects from compute_network() or as_network(), one entry per species.

block

Named list of per-sample factors, one per species in expr. Each species is split with split_layers(). The network is built from the wiring layer.

clades

Named list of species vectors, one per clade, as for classify_gene_cliques(). NULL skips the clade tiers.

density

Fraction of gene pairs kept as edges in each network.

sign

"positive" or "negative": the correlation sign that makes an edge. See compute_network().

method

"hypergeometric" or "rank": the test of each ortholog pair. See find_coexpressologs().

alpha

The q-value threshold for a call.

modules

If TRUE, detect modules in each species and test their preservation in every species pair.

null

If TRUE, repeat the run with hog labels shuffled among genes of the same expression level. The null calls and tiers estimate what abundance and network structure alone produce.

n_cores

Number of threads.

seed

Integer seed, or NULL to draw from the global stream. A seed makes the run reproducible and leaves your stream unchanged.

Value

A list of class rcomplex:

networks

The network objects, by species.

edges

The edge table from find_coexpressologs(), plus a sign column: the sign of every network.

cliques, members, twins

The three tables of gene_clique_graph(): one row per clique, one row per clique member, and one row per collapsed twin gene. The tables of the three graphs are stacked. run numbers the graph: 1 strict, 2 loose, 3 all tested pairs. alpha_graph holds its cut: alpha, 0.9 or Inf. clique_id counts within a run, so run and clique_id together name a clique.

capped

One row per hog and run over the clique budget of gene_clique_graph(), with run and alpha_graph. Its cliques are species blocks. Usually empty.

classification

One row per clique, from classify_gene_cliques(). Its run and clique_id join cliques and members.

modules, preservation

With modules = TRUE: the detect_modules() results by species, and the preservation_paired() result.

edges_null, classification_null

With null = TRUE: the edge table and the classification of the shuffled ortholog table.

call

The call.

as.data.frame() returns the classification.

Details

The driver lists cliques on three gene graphs. The strict graph holds the edges with q_value < alpha. It feeds complete_conserved, lineage_specific, partial_present and trait_specific. The loose graph holds the edges with q_value < 0.9. It feeds partial_significant. The third graph holds every tested pair. It covers only the hogs with no complete or partial tier on the first two graphs. It feeds differentiated, as does the loose graph where every cross pair has q_value < 0.9. classify_gene_cliques() classifies the three graphs together, so hog_class reads all of them. A clique maximal on two graphs appears once for each. The third graph is built only with clades, since only the clade tiers read it.

Every clique has at least min(3, number of species) genes. Rank edges are classified at min_power = 0.9, hypergeometric edges at 0.8.

density and sign apply only to networks built from expr. method = "rank" and block need expr. The rank test calibrates against null_network() partners, built within each block.

summary() counts each tier in cliques, in hogs and in patterns. A pattern is one HOG with one clique species set. The paralog copies of a large HOG can form millions of cliques, but they share a few patterns. Paralogs with the same partners are twins: one clique stands for all their combinations. The multiplicity column counts those combinations, and twins lists the collapsed genes.

With null = TRUE, the driver shuffles the gene column of orthologs within each species. A gene moves only among genes of the same expression decile, by gene_mean from compute_network(). A network without gene_mean, such as one from as_network(), forms one decile. The driver then reruns edges, cliques and tiers on the real networks. Both runs share the rank calibration networks.

With null = TRUE, summary() reports calls and calls_null per species pair at q_value < alpha. Their ratio is the empirical false-call rate. The rate is NA for a species pair without calls. The tier table gains cliques_null: the null cliques per tier.

print() counts the cliques of each graph. It shows, per species, the genes, the samples, the density and r_threshold from compute_network(): the weakest correlation that passed the density threshold. The same density needs a stronger correlation at few samples. A network from as_network() has no correlation and shows r ?, as does a network without edges.

Examples

f <- function(x) system.file("extdata", x, package = "rcomplex")
read <- function(x) as.matrix(read.delim(f(x), row.names = 1L))
expr <- lapply(c(SpA = "expr_sp1_small.txt", SpB = "expr_sp2_small.txt"),
  read)
res <- rcomplex(expr, f("orthologs_small.txt"), density = 0.1, seed = 1)
res
#> rcomplex: 2 species, 10 hogs, 0 tiers
#>   SpA  50 genes  10 samples  density 0.1  r >= 0.30
#>   SpB  40 genes  10 samples  density 0.1  r >= 0.23
#>   edges 12 tested, 0 called at q < 0.1
#>   graphs: 0 cliques at q < 0.1, 0 at q < 0.9
#>   cliques 0
summary(res)
#> [1] tier         cliques      cliques_null multiplicity hogs        
#> [6] patterns    
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
#> null: not run
write_rcomplex(res, tempfile())
